Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

GiottoConnect 0.1.0

Bug fixes

  • giottoToSeurat() no longer drops features whose names contain _ from every layer but counts and from the feature metadata. Seurat renames _ to -; all layers and the feature metadata now get the same names, and features that would collide after the rename stop the export.

Converters

  • giottoToAnnData() writes one spatial unit and feature type of a giotto object (in memory or GiottoDisk-backed) as an .h5ad in scanpy’s layout, without python (anndataR): normalized values in X, counts in layers/counts, other values as layers, reductions in obsm (PCA loadings in varm/PCs), nn and spatial networks in obsp with a uns record. anndataToGiotto() reads them back under their Giotto names, and also reads every scanpy/squidpy network and extra layer of other files.
  • giottoToSeurat() takes spat_unit / feat_type and exports every reduction (with PCA loadings and stdev), every nearest-neighbour network as a Graph, and transcripts as FOV molecules.
  • giottoToSpatialExperiment() converts one spatial unit and feature type to a SpatialExperiment, or a SpatialFeatureExperiment when there are polygons, transcripts or spatial networks: counts / logcounts and other assays, scater-named reductions with PCA loadings, networks as colPairs (and SFE spatialGraphs), polygons as cellSeg, transcripts as txSpots. spatialExperimentToGiotto() reads them back under their Giotto names.
  • Tissue images go both ways. Seurat Visium images, SpatialExperiment imgData and scanpy uns/spatial images become Giotto images placed in the spot coordinates; giottoToSeurat() writes a VisiumV2 (so SpatialFeaturePlot() shows the tissue), giottoToSpatialExperiment() an imgData image and giottoToAnnData() a scanpy uns/spatial library.
  • seuratToGiotto() reads every nearest-neighbour Graph, not only the first.
  • spatialExperimentToGiotto() converts SpatialExperiment and SpatialFeatureExperiment objects through the same mapping engine: the layouts of SpatialExperimentIO (Xenium, CosMx, MERSCOPE), VisiumIO (Visium, Visium HD; pixels converted to microns) and SpatialFeatureExperiment (cell and nucleus segmentations, transcripts, spatial graphs). Control probes, as altExps or inside the main matrix, become their own feature types; scater PCA loadings and variances are kept.
  • seuratToGiotto() and anndataToGiotto() convert with a declarative mapping chosen for the object’s structure, not per object version. Bundled mappings cover Seurat v3/v4 and v5 assays with FOV, Visium (V1, V2, HD) or Slide-seq images, and AnnData .h5ad files from scanpy/squidpy (read with hdf5r, no python).
  • Converted: expression (every assay or feature_types category as its own feature type), cell and feature metadata, spatial locations, polygons, transcripts (Seurat FOV molecules), dimension reductions with PCA loadings and eigenvalues, nearest-neighbour networks and squidpy spatial networks.
  • source = builds a GiottoDisk-backed object; AnnData matrices stream from the file.
  • mappingProvenance() records the mapping, bound parameters, losses, absent parts and fallback sources used; readbackCheck() compares the result with the source.
  • Lower-level tools: findMapping(), convertWithMapping(), validateMapping(), repairMapping(), profileObject(), giottoContract().

External tools

  • runSparkX() runs SPARK-X (SPARK package, GitHub) for spatially variable genes on counts and stores its combined and Benjamini-Yekutieli adjusted p-values as feature metadata (sparkxParam() for analyzeData()). Use it in place of Giotto’s spark(), which runs the original SPARK model.

  • runScrublet() runs Scrublet doublet detection on counts and stores each cell’s score and call as cell metadata (scrubletParam() for analyzeData()); the Python package is installed with reticulate::py_require() on first use, no conda. It replaces Giotto’s doScrubletDetect(), with the same scores. When Scrublet cannot set a score threshold (e.g. on spots) only the scores are stored, with a warning; scrubletParam(threshold =) sets one.

  • Banksy, BayesSpace, CellChat, nnSVG and ONTraC declare their papers (GiottoClass::methodCitation()): the citation is shown once per session when the tool runs and GiottoClass::objCitations() lists it. checkGiottoMethod() checks that a param declares one (cite = FALSE for Suite-native methods that wrap no published method).

  • runMAST() runs MAST for marker features between clusters, either one comparison (group_1 against group_2) or each cluster against the others, and returns MAST’s hurdle test per feature (mastParam() for analyzeData()). It replaces Giotto’s findMastMarkers() and findMastMarkers_one_vs_all() with the same results. MAST is in Suggests.

  • Python tools (Scrublet, ONTraC) run in a worker R session through GiottoUtils::py_run(), each in its own uv environment, so they run in one R session in any order and the session itself never starts Python. options(giotto.py_python =) points them at an own Python instead. The Python and package versions they used are stored with their parameters in the giotto object (py_versions).

Dependencies

  • reticulate moves to Suggests: only the Bento and SpatialData converters and the python tools (ONTraC, Scrublet) use it, and they check for it when they run.
  • Requires GiottoClass 0.8.0 (methodCitation()) and GiottoUtils 0.2.11 (py_run()).

Removed

  • gefToGiotto(): Giotto’s importStereoSeq() (and GiottoDisk’s importStereoSeqDisk()) read Stereo-seq GEF files. rhdf5 is no longer suggested.
  • seuratToGiottoV4(), seuratToGiottoV5(), giottoToSeuratV4(), giottoToSeuratV5() (use seuratToGiotto() / giottoToSeurat()).
  • giottoToSpatialData(), and the reticulate-based giottoToAnnData() (replaced by the one above); anndataToGiotto() no longer needs python.
  • The Vitessce site pipeline (export_giotto_to_zarr(), create_vitessce_config(), scaffold_vitessce_site(), giotto_to_vitessce_site(), setup_giotto_connect_env()).
